reference: GNU coreutils cksum invoked by name in the isolated reference PATH. Its POSIX CRC-32 mode and supported GNU digest modes are the independent behavioral oracle; reference status is checked before candidate parity is reported.
coverage: POSIX CRC-32 output for named files and stdin
Empty and binary inputs, including the byte count
Multiple files, stdin in an argument list, and -- for dash-leading names
All six documented digest algorithms, tagged and untagged formats, and digest stdin
Missing-file continuation and invalid algorithm/option errors
Explicit dash operands retain their name, including repeated EOF and NUL-delimited records.
Same-shell parser failures leave input unread and reset options for later invocations.
Missing/directory/closed-input failures retain failure status while later checksums work.
--check over tagged lines of every supported digest and untagged lines with -a, with --quiet/--status/--strict/--warn/--ignore-missing and GNU option conflicts; blake2b digests (guest pass 3 G47)
exclusions: GNU --raw, --base64, --length, legacy sysv/bsd/crc32b modes, and algorithms outside the documented set
Version banner identity and exact diagnostic wording
Very large inputs beyond the harness fixture limits

cases.purpose: Compare POSIX CRC-32 and byte counts for the same small text input as a named file and as stdin; the named form must include the filename while stdin must omit it.
cases.script:
printf 'abc\n' > plain
cksum plain
cksum < plain

cases.purpose: Exercise the zero-byte boundary and non-text bytes so the CRC and reported byte count are checked independently of line-oriented input.
cases.script:
: > empty
printf '\000\377A\n' > binary
cksum empty binary
cksum < empty

cases.purpose: Check ordered output for multiple operands with stdin between two files, including a binary file payload.
cases.script:
printf 'first\n' > first
printf 'last\000byte' > last
printf 'stream\001bytes' | cksum first - last

cases.purpose: Verify that -- ends option parsing so a dash-leading relative filename is opened and printed as a filename.
cases.script:
printf 'dash-name\n' > ./-payload
cksum -- -payload

cases.purpose: Compare NUL-terminated checksum records for a filename containing a space and an empty file.
cases.script:
printf 'space name data\n' > 'space name'
: > empty
cksum --zero -- 'space name' empty

cases.purpose: Compare GNU digest output for every digest algorithm documented by this loadable against deterministic binary input.
cases.script:
printf 'digest\000payload\377\n' > payload
for alg in md5 sha1 sha224 sha256 sha384 sha512; do cksum --algorithm="$alg" payload; done

cases.purpose: Check default tagged and explicit --tag output, --untagged output, the documented '-' name for digest stdin, and NUL termination for an untagged digest record.
cases.script:
printf 'sha input\n' > payload
printf 'zero delimiter\n' > 'space name'
cksum -a sha256 payload
cksum --tag --algorithm sha256 payload
cksum --untagged --algorithm=sha256 payload
cksum --untagged -a sha256 < payload
cksum -z --untagged -a sha1 -- 'space name'

cases.purpose: Ensure a missing operand reports an error and sets failure status while a later readable file still produces its checksum.
cases.script:
printf 'readable\n' > present
if cksum absent present; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
exit "$rc"

cases.purpose: Compare failure status and nonempty diagnostics for an unsupported algorithm name.
cases.script: cksum --algorithm=not-a-real-algorithm

cases.purpose: Compare failure status and nonempty diagnostics for an unknown option.
cases.script: cksum --not-a-real-option

cases.purpose: Check output for a relative filename containing a newline, where escaping or raw-name handling can affect checksum record bytes.
cases.script:
name=$'line\nbreak'
printf 'newline path\n' > "$name"
cksum "$name"

cases.purpose: Check Bash metadata only: cksum is a builtin and help output includes the documented POSIX CRC-32 summary.
cases.script:
type -t cksum
help cksum > help.txt
found=no
while IFS= read -r line; do case $line in *'POSIX CRC-32'*) found=yes ;; esac; done < help.txt
[[ $found == yes ]]
printf 'help summary present\n'

cases.purpose: An explicit stdin operand is named dash; default stdin omits its name. Repeated dash operands see EOF on the second read, and zero mode keeps exact record delimiters.
cases.script:
printf 'abc' | cksum -
printf 'abc' | cksum
printf 'A\000B' | cksum -z - -

cases.purpose: Repeated reads in one shell preserve descriptor ownership, observe EOF, accept a fresh redirection, and reset digest selection to CRC on a later call.
cases.script:
printf 'abc' > plain
{ cksum - -; cksum; } < plain
cksum < plain
cksum -a sha256 plain
cksum plain

cases.purpose: Missing algorithm and unsupported algorithm errors return 1 before reading stdin; zero/digest options do not leak into a later same-shell invocation.
cases.script:
printf 'abc' > plain
{
 rc=0; cksum -a || rc=$?
 [[ $rc == 1 ]]
 printf 'missing-algorithm=%s\n' "$rc"
 rc=0; cksum -z --algorithm=not-a-real-algorithm || rc=$?
 [[ $rc == 1 ]]
 printf 'unsupported=%s\n' "$rc"
 cksum
} < plain
cksum --untagged -a sha256 plain
cksum plain

cases.purpose: Missing operands and directory read errors continue to stdin and valid files; CRC and digest closed-input failures return 1 and leave later invocations usable.
cases.script:
mkdir folder
printf 'abc' > present
rc=0; cksum absent folder - present < present || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
printf 'operands=%s\n' "$rc"
rc=0; cksum <&- || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
rc=0; cksum -a sha256 <&- || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
printf 'closed-inputs-rejected\n'
cksum present

cases.purpose: cksum --check verifies tagged lines of any digest (including BLAKE2b and upper-case hex) and, with -a, untagged lines of that algorithm; mismatches, malformed lines and missing files are reported as GNU cksum does (guest pass 3 G47).
cases.script:
printf 'a\n' > a; printf 'b\n' > b
s() { local rc=0; "$@" || rc=$?; echo "rc=$rc"; }
cksum -a sha256 a > c; cksum -a md5 b >> c; cksum -a blake2b a >> c; cksum -a sha1 b >> c
s cksum --check c; s cksum -c --quiet c; s cksum -c --status c
cksum -a sha512 --untagged a > u; s cksum -a sha512 -c u; s cksum -c u; s cksum -a sha256 -c c
printf 'SHA256 (a) = %064d\njunk\n' 0 > bad; s cksum -c bad; s cksum -c -w bad; s cksum -c --strict c bad
printf 'SHA256 (zz) = %064d\n' 0 > miss; s cksum -c miss; s cksum -c --ignore-missing miss; cat miss c > mix; s cksum -c --ignore-missing mix
s cksum -c < c

cases.purpose: Check-only options without --check, --tag or -z with --check, and --check with the CRC algorithm exit 1.
cksum -a blake2b prints the BSD-tagged BLAKE2b-512 digest and --untagged the plain form.
cases.script: printf 'abc' > f; cksum -a blake2b f; cksum -a blake2b --untagged f; printf '' | cksum -a blake2b

cases.purpose: Guest pass 4 G68: cksum -a blake2b -l/--length BITS computes the shorter BLAKE2b digest (not a truncation), tags it BLAKE2b-BITS, treats 0 and values over 512 as 512, and verifies the tagged and untagged lines it writes.
cases.script:
printf 'abc' > f; cksum -a blake2b -l 256 f; cksum -a blake2b --length=16 --untagged f; cksum -a blake2b -l8 f; cksum -a blake2b -l 0 f; cksum -a blake2b -l 1024 --untagged f
cksum -a blake2b -l 256 f > c; cksum -c c; cksum -a blake2b -l 256 --untagged f > u; cksum -a blake2b -c u

cases.purpose: -l needs blake2b and a decimal multiple of 8; other values fail with status 1.
cases.script:
s() { local rc=0; "$@" || rc=$?; echo "rc=$rc"; }
printf 'abc' > f; s cksum -l 16 f; s cksum -a sha256 -l 16 f; s cksum -a blake2b -l 7 f; s cksum -a blake2b -l abc f; s cksum -a blake2b -l -8 f

cases.purpose: cksum --base64 prints digests in base64 (tagged and --untagged; ignored for the CRC), --raw writes the binary digest (CRC: 4 bytes big-endian) for one file only, the two are mutually exclusive, and -c reads base64 digests (guest pass 7, G112).
cases.script:
s() { local rc=0; eval "$1" 2>&1 || rc=$?; echo "rc=$rc"; }
printf '' > e; echo hi > h
s 'cksum -a sha256 --base64 e'
s 'cksum -a sha256 --base64 --untagged e'
s 'cksum -a md5 --base64 e h'
s 'cksum -a blake2b -l 128 --base64 e'
s 'cksum -a blake2b -l 128 --base64 --untagged e'
s 'cksum --base64 e'
s 'cksum -a sha256 --raw e | od -An -tx1'
s 'cksum -a sha256 --raw e h'
s 'cksum --raw e | od -An -tx1'
s 'cksum --raw < h | od -An -tx1'
s 'cksum -a sha1 --raw --tag e | od -An -tx1'
s 'cksum -a sha1 --raw --base64 e'
s 'cksum -a sha1 --base64 -z e | od -An -c'
s 'cksum -a sha512 --raw < e | wc -c'

cases.purpose: cksum -c verifies tagged and untagged base64 digests (BLAKE2b tagged at any length; an untagged base64 BLAKE2b line is improperly formatted, as in GNU) and reports a wrong one as FAILED (guest pass 7, G112).
cases.script:
s() { local rc=0; eval "$1" 2>&1 || rc=$?; echo "rc=$rc"; }
echo hi > h
s 'cksum -a sha256 --base64 h > b64; cksum -c b64'
s 'cksum -a sha256 --base64 --untagged h > b64u; cksum -a sha256 -c b64u'
s 'cksum -a blake2b --base64 h > b2; cksum -c b2'
s 'cksum -a blake2b --base64 --untagged h > b2u; cksum -a blake2b -c b2u'
s 'cksum -a blake2b -l 256 --base64 h > b3; cksum -c b3'
s 'cksum -a md5 --base64 h | sed '"'"'s/= .*/= AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA==/'"'"' > bad; cksum -c bad'
s 'cksum -a md5 --base64 h | sed '"'"'s/==$/=x/'"'"' > bad2; cksum -c bad2'

cases.purpose: cksum -c summaries in GNU's order and wording: "WARNING: 1 line is improperly formatted" / "N lines are", "no properly formatted checksum lines found" even under --status, open errors printed under --status, --ignore-missing silences only missing files (guest pass 7, G105).
cases.script:
s() { local rc=0; eval "$1" 2>&1 || rc=$?; echo "rc=$rc"; }
echo 1 > a; cksum -a sha256 a > k; cp k k2; echo junk >> k; echo junk >> k2; echo junk >> k2; cksum -a sha256 a | sed 's/ a)/ a5)/' > k5; cat k > k5x; cat k5 >> k5x; echo junk > k7
s 'cksum -c k'
s 'cksum -c k2'
s 'cksum -c --ignore-missing k5x'
s 'cksum -c --status k7'
s 'cksum -c --status nosuch'
s 'cksum -c --status k5'
